verdict.rationale: Galileo documents its own tracing: its SDK, the `@log` decorator and OTel integrations capture every session, trace and span for LLM calls across the major providers. The evidence never explicitly says these traces record inputs, outputs, latency or token usage; only a cost-based alert hints at usage tracking. missing for 10: explicit documentation of captured input/output payloads, latency and token-count fields on spans, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can capture traces of my LLM calls with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage

citations.quote: Once instrumented, Galileo captures every session, trace, and span, producing a structured stream of real-time data.
You can also use the `@log` decorator to log spans.
Learn how to log your first trace with Galileo
This guide works with Python or TypeScript, using OpenAI, Azure OpenAI service, Anthropic, or Gemini LLMs.
Learn how to instrument a LangGraph agent with OpenTelemetry and OpenInference to capture detailed traces, spans, and metrics.
